en-US.author: Will Lehnertz
en-US.longDescription:
Baudrun is a cross-platform (macOS + Windows + Linux) serial
terminal for network devices. Built for switch consoles, router
CLIs, and other serial-attached gear.

Profile-based: each device gets a named profile storing port,
baud rate, framing, flow control, line ending, and optional
send-on-connect sequences. One-click connect; no
`screen /dev/cu.usbserial-...` from memory.
en-US.name: Baudrun
en-US.releaseNotes:
Highlights
A Sidebar Glass skin, matched to zorite's, and custom baud rates are back.
Added
- Sidebar Glass skin. The sidebar, title bar and status bar show the
  OS blur (vibrancy on macOS, acrylic on Windows, the compositor's blur on
  Linux) while the content stays opaque, like macOS sidebars. Light and
  dark. Custom skins opt in with --window-blur: on.
Fixed
- Custom baud rates are back. The baud dropdown has a Custom…
  entry again (lost in the move from Tauri); pick it and type any rate
  your adapter supports.
- macOS ptys connect. Ports like /dev/ttys010 (the
  virtual-serial test bridge, socat) failed with "Not a typewriter";
  Baudrun now skips setting the speed on them.
What's Changed
- ci(release): make the extracted AppDir readable for appimagetool (88210da)
- docs(changelog): cut v0.17.0 — Sidebar Glass (58eba41)

- fix(skins): match Sidebar Glass to zorite's (33eaaaa)
- fix(skins): Sidebar Glass borders follow the blur (fb735ec)
- fix(editor): restore the Custom… baud rate option (d7a7707)
